ContentElementId.title: Content element id
ContentElementId.description: Element identifier. Any non-empty string is accepted except the reserved root literal `__page_context_root__` and strings PHP casts to integers (`0`, `12`, `-3`); apart from those two exclusions the id is stored verbatim, with no format, length or character-set requirement, so an author-supplied id such as `el-1` is as valid as a generated hex id. The reserved literal is minted by the render-time page-context wrapper, so an authored element carrying it collides with the wrapper; an integer-castable id would turn the string-keyed per-element maps of a response into JSON lists. Both are rejected with `400`. The `pattern` is marginally stricter than the server on two inputs the server does accept — `-0` and digit strings past PHP integer range — because a regular expression cannot express a platform-dependent integer bound.
